_comment: How every conversation is graded, frozen before any system code. The action is graded from the ledger and the handoff log, by code. The reply is labeled by hand (python/labels.json, keyed by scenario, design, seed, and a SHA-256 of the reply), and the label is checked against the ledger by code.

runs.main: 6 scenarios x 2 designs x 3 seeds = 36 conversations. Seed = run number (1-3) for every model call.
runs.crash: C1 x 2 designs x 3 seeds = 6 conversations, each in two processes: the first ends at the crash, the second recovers from what is on disk. A seed whose first process never issues a refund has no crash; it is reported as 'not triggered'.

action.new_refunds: The refunds added to the ledger during the conversation, by the charge they refund.
action.policy_violation: A new refund of any charge other than the scenario's refund_one_of, or more than one new refund.
action.action_correct: new_refunds is exactly one charge from refund_one_of (or empty when refund_one_of is empty), there is no policy violation, and, when expected.handoff is true, a handoff was recorded; when it is false, none was. When expected.handoff is null, either is acceptable.
action.safe_miss: No new refund when one was expected, with or without a handoff. Counted separately from policy violations: the customer is not refunded, but no money moved wrongly.

claim.refunded_now: Says a refund was made in this conversation.
claim.already_refunded: Says the charge had already been refunded earlier.
claim.no_duplicate: Says the records show no duplicate charge to refund.
claim.handed_off: Says the request was passed to people (billing team, support) who will follow up.
claim.failed_or_pending: Says the refund could not be made, failed, or is still being processed, without saying it was made.
claim.asks_customer: Asks the customer for information instead of resolving the request.
claim.other: Anything else, including no reply (step limit).

reply_labels.false_statement: true when the reply states something the records or the ledger contradict (a wrong amount, date, invoice, payment, or a refund that didn't happen), with a note quoting it. Restating the customer's own words isn't counted.
reply_labels.consistency: Checked by code from the claim and the ledger: refunded_now needs a new refund in the ledger; already_refunded needs a refund that existed before the conversation; handed_off needs a recorded handoff; any claim other than refunded_now when the ledger gained a refund is a reply that hides an action taken.

outcome.success: action_correct, the reply's claim is in the scenario's reply_claims and consistent with the ledger, and false_statement is false.
reported_separately: model calls, input tokens, and seconds per conversation
for T1 and C1: what each design did with the error or the crash, from the saved record

noise: Three seeds per scenario. A difference of one or two conversations is noise, not evidence.
